source: GeoNames modern P-class identity/coordinates, Store norske leksikon, local Izhevsk news, Russian Soviet Historical Encyclopedia, Kavkazskiy Uzel, Presidential Library original 1943 decree, Columbia Encyclopedia and Drevo city histories.
selection: 23 distinct Russian regional cities, screened against all 1–23 existing GeoNames IDs. Only independently source-reviewed historical names are runtime candidates; relocation, merged city identity and disputable name chronology held.
coordinateConvention: Modern GeoNames EPSG:4326 representative coordinate; historic city position may differ.
countryCodeSemantics: RU metadata refers to current Geonames classification, not historical sovereignty.
historicNameScope: Attested sustained official names only; exact dates not inferred. A records' 1801 modern labels are provisional editorial placeholders, not historical validation.
reviewMethod: Cross-checked ID uniqueness against batches 01–23, verified contemporary GeoNames P-class coordinates, selected independently sourced rename timelines and withheld A and urban-identity disputes.
qualityNotes: Novokuznetsk 1932 merger requires distinct geohistorical identity review.
Tolyatti modern site differs from submerged historical city.
Elista, Ivanovo and Naberezhnye Chelny before-city-foundation labels suppressed.
